clue.text: Boiler going in benefits root crop

indicators.note: the boiler is said to be going in, so it sits inside the word for benefits

parts.note: tips are perks or gratuities, benefits on top of pay
an urn is a large vessel for boiling water

explanation.surface: A boiler installation comes with perks, oddly linked to a farm vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in' is the insertion signal: the boiler goes into the benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnips are a vegetable grown for their swollen edible roots.

clue.text: Where climbers go on horseback with notices about river

parts.note: a jockey who is riding is said to be up

indicators.note: about means the notices go around the abbreviation for river

parts.note: ads are advertisements, notices

explanation.surface: Climbers set off on horseback carrying posters about a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside ADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers head upwards, towards the summit, so the adverb names their direction.

clue.text: Immature flyer's city rate

parts.note: NY is New York City
mph, miles per hour, is a rate of speed

explanation.surface: A young pilot complains about the speed limit in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' suggests a pilot; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymph is the young stage of insects such as dragonflies before they become winged adults.

clue.text: Staff not available to collect first of the dough

parts.note: a pole is a staff or stick

indicators.note: to collect means the abbreviation gathers in the next letter
first of picks the opening letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Staff unavailable to pick up the first of the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' suggests money; 'to collect' puts T inside NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is a thick cornmeal paste, a dough-like Italian staple.

clue.text: Pilfer a couple of books in Coop

indicators.note: the letters for a couple of books are placed in the word for coop

parts.note: a coop is an enclosure for birds, a cage
B is an abbreviation for book, so two of them give BB

explanation.surface: Someone steals a couple of books from the Co-op shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Coop' suggests the Co-op, a British chain of shops; here it is just a bird enclosure, and 'in' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbage is old British slang for stealing, originally tailors keeping leftover cloth.

clue.text: Indecisive prince heading off to secure king's band

indicators.note: to secure means the shortened name holds the next letter inside it
heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Hamlet is Shakespeare's famously indecisive Prince of Denmark
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A dithering prince sets off to fasten a king's band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves AMLET; 'to secure' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band worn around the upper arm.

clue.text: Decline flattens out finances

parts.note: a bank is a slope, a decline in the ground
to roll out dough is to flatten it

explanation.surface: An economic decline squashes a company's finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finances' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bankroll a project is to fund it, so bankrolls means pays for.

clue.text: Cook laughs about duck stew

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the letter for duck
to cook something up is to concoct it, so these letters are concocted afresh

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A cook laughs over a duck stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges LAUGHS into GULASH; 'about' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian meat stew seasoned with paprika.

clue.text: Wild garlic chokes posh traveller but not ordinary farmer

indicators.note: chokes means the rearranged letters grip the letter for posh inside them
wild means untamed and disordered, so these letters run riot

parts.note: U is short for upper class, posh

indicators.note: but not means the next letter is left out of the traveller

parts.note: a tourist is a traveller

explanation.surface: Wild garlic overwhelms a well-heeled traveller but not a plain farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges the garlic into AGRICL, which 'chokes' the posh letter to give AGRICUL; 'but not' drops the ordinary letter from the traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: An agriculturist practises or studies farming.

clue.text: Regularly saw firms dip

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter from the words saw and firms, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A report that firms took a regular dip, as in sales figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'saw firms'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip is a short swim, as in a quick dip in the sea.

clue.text: Like pulse clear, say, when admitted

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say is admitted, let in, to the word for clear

parts.note: luminous means bright and clear
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A medical remark about a pulse that is clear when a patient is admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat; it is the bean family. 'when admitted' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses such as lentils and peas belong to the legume family, so leguminous describes them.

clue.text: Seafood devoured by four Chinooks

indicators.note: the answer is swallowed up inside the letters of the words four Chinooks

explanation.surface: Four Chinook salmon gobble up some seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through fo(UR CHIN)ooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea urchins are spiny sea creatures whose roe is eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Dispatch 100 papers showing scoop maybe?

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for killing them, dispatching them
C is the Roman numeral for 100
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A newspaper sends off a hundred papers carrying a scoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoop' plays on a newspaper exclusive; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is served in scoops, so a scoop is one example of it.

clue.text: A small South American country's exporting a Yankee vegetable

indicators.note: exporting means sending out, so these letters leave the country's name

parts.note: Paraguay is a South American country, with the 's adding S
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A small South American nation exports a Yankee-grown vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exporting' removes A and Y from PARAGUAYS, leaving PARAGUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a vegetable eaten for its young green spears.

clue.text: A pair of students and old workers fill dry beds here

parts.note: L for learner, as on a British L-plate, doubled

indicators.note: fill means the workers go inside the letters for dry

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry
men are workers, a staff

explanation.surface: Students and old workers tend dry flowerbeds on a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fill' is the insertion signal. An allotment is a small rented plot for growing vegetables, common in Britain; L for learner comes from British L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetable beds are laid out on an allotment, so it is where such beds are.

clue.text: Brightest star first in list including Charlie and Mike

definitions.meaning: the brightest star in a constellation is designated ..., as ... Centauri

definitions.text: first in list including Charlie and Mike
definitions.meaning: The first word of the NATO phonetic alphabet, which includes Charlie and Mike

explanation.surface: A celebrity tops a guest list that includes Charlie and Mike.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers label a constellation's brightest star with the Greek letter for A, which also opens the radio alphabet.

clue.text: Cow's beef, pickled

definitions.meaning: ... beef is pickled or corned beef

explanation.surface: A cow's meat turns out to be pickled beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is a verb, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to browbeat them, and bully beef is tinned corned meat.

clue.text: Free, like a new bass?

definitions.meaning: a new double bass has not yet been played with a bow, so it is the answer

explanation.surface: A question whether a new bass is as free as it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbowed means undefeated and unsubjugated; punningly it is an instrument never touched by a bow.

clue.text: Shepherd uses goat with rare old herbivore

indicators.note: to shepherd is to herd and marshal, so these letters are herded into a new order

explanation.surface: A shepherd uses a goat along with some rare ancient grazing beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The stegosaurus was a plant-eating dinosaur that lived millions of years ago.

clue.text: Greek cross about a very large area for salmon

indicators.note: about means Greek and cross together go around what follows

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A cross Greek complains about a very large area set aside for salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AVLA between GR and X.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravlax is Scandinavian salmon cured with salt, sugar and dill.

clue.text: European city's butter's occasionally genuine

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every second letter of the word is taken

parts.note: echt is German, also used in English, for genuine or authentic

explanation.surface: A European city's butter is only sometimes the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of butter's.
explanation.definitionFit: Utrecht is a city in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Unfinished volumes slip

indicators.note: unfinished means each item lacks its last letter

parts.note: two volumes are two books

explanation.surface: Leaving books incomplete is a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: Each BOOK of the plural 'volumes' loses its last letter: BOO + BOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A booboo is an informal word for a silly mistake or slip.

clue.text: Boar at it gets butchered

indicators.note: butchered means chopped up, so the letters of boar at it are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A boar is slaughtered at the place in question.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a slaughterhouse is where a boar gets butchered.
explanation.definitionFit: An abattoir is a slaughterhouse, where animals such as boars are killed for meat.

clue.text: Have avoided astringent dessert

indicators.note: avoided means steered clear of, so the word have is left out

parts.note: aftershave is an astringent lotion

explanation.surface: Someone has dodged a sharp-tasting pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astringent' is a noun here, a skin lotion; 'avoided' removes HAVE from AFTERSHAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is informal British for the pudding course that comes after the main meal.

clue.text: King Edward, say, initially took over in Germany

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of took is taken

parts.note: über is German for over

explanation.surface: King Edward first seized power over a territory in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British variety of potato, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a tuber, and King Edward is an example of a potato variety.

clue.text: Not how Sybil referred to her husband, Herb!

definitions.text: Not how Sybil referred to her husband
definitions.meaning: in the sitcom Fawlty Towers Sybil Fawlty is endlessly sharp with her husband Basil, never calling him sweet
a culinary herb used in Italian cooking

explanation.surface: A wry aside that Sybil never sweet-talked her husband, Herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a classic British sitcom in which hotelier Basil Fawlty is nagged by his wife Sybil. 'Herb' looks like the husband's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet basil is the common culinary variety of the aromatic plant used in pesto.

clue.text: Scots vomit almost swallowing cold drink in Bonn

indicators.note: swallowing means the shortened word takes in the next letter
almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: boke is a Scots word for vomit or retch

explanation.surface: A Scot nearly throws up after a cold drink in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BOKE to BOK; 'swallowing' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bock is a strong German lager, the sort of beer drunk in a German city.

clue.text: Issue subversive speech with no introduction

indicators.note: having no introduction means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: sedition is speech inciting rebellion against authority

explanation.surface: A publication brings out an inflammatory speech without a preface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no introduction' takes the S off SEDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one printed issue of a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Evacuate middle of next island

indicators.note: the middle of a four-letter word is its two central letters

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: An order to clear people out of the centre of the next island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes EX from nEXt.
explanation.definitionFit: To evacuate one's bowels is to excrete, discharging waste from the body.
